subject: Request: temporary priority uplift & SLA addendum for Sundial Health
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sundial Health Platform <platform@sundialhealth.com>, Procurement <procure@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request: temporary throughput uplift for launch week

Hi David,

We're kicking off the Sundial Health pilot next Monday and expect an initial spike in inference traffic for our triage workflows. Our SRE team estimates a 4-6x burst for a 48-hour window during the first week of the pilot. Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift to the rate cap / burst allowance and an SLA addendum that covers latency and availability for that window? Procurement also needs a short-term doc we can attach to the contract that describes the scope and any pricing delta.

Key details:
- Expected peak: ~6k requests/min peak, baseline ~1.2k/min
- Typical sequence length: 512 tokens (mostly text + structured fields)
- Region: us-west
- Pilot window: 2028-03-06 to 2028-03-08 (48 hours)

I've attached our traffic snapshot for the past 7 days and the procurement intake form. Can you confirm feasibility and any lead time required?

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Director of Platform Engineering
Sundial Health

Attachments: traffic_report_q1.csv, sundial_procurement_form.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Sundial Health Platform <platform@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary throughput uplift for launch week

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. Short answer: we can support a temporary uplift, but we'll need to coordinate a couple of operational and contractual items. Looping in Neha (SE) and Priyom (AM) to scope the technical profile and to get a brief addendum drafted.

Immediate questions for Sundial:
1) Is the 6k req/min sustained across the 48 hours or spike-and-decay (e.g., several 10–20 min spikes)?
2) Do you need guaranteed token-level latency SLOs (p95/p99) or an availability SLA tied to a higher priority lane?
3) Any regulatory constraints (PHI) that should change routing/region choices?

We'll aim to propose two options by EOD tomorrow:
- Option A: Reserved burst pool (guaranteed tokens during window) + SLA addendum for availability
- Option B: Best-effort uplift with monitored fairshare adjustments (lower cost, no formal availability SLA)

David
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Mar 1, 2028 at 09:12 AM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com> wrote:
> We're kicking off the Sundial Health pilot next Monday... (see below)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary throughput uplift for launch week

Alex — thanks, I reviewed the traffic snapshot. A few technical notes and a recommended configuration: 

Technical readout:
- 512 token median; tail up to ~1k tokens in ~12% of requests
- Baseline concurrency looks like 80–100 connections, spikes top to ~480

Suggested mitigations (we can combine):
1) Priority token pool (reserved capacity) for the 48-hour window: pre-provision N tokens/sec to avoid fairshare preemption.
2) Short-lived canary route: route 15% of traffic through a dedicated model variant with lower quantization to lower latency during the window.
3) Prefix/KV cache warm-up 24h prior to launch to reduce first-token latency.

Monitoring & SLOs: we can commit to p95 < 220ms and p99 < 450ms for requests served from the reserved pool. For best-effort lifts we only guarantee p95 < 350ms. Full latency breakdowns will be available in the Console.

Operational ask: please confirm an expected peak-minute profile (e.g., 6k for 10 minutes every hour vs continuous). That will determine the size of the priority pool and the cost delta. I attached a small CSV template we use to size the pool; fill in if you have per-minute estimates.

-Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Mar 1, 2028 at 10:03 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Alex — thanks for the heads up...

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 08:39:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary throughput uplift for launch week

Alex — quick note from the contracts side. Based on Neha's recommended reserved priority pool and the SLA numbers, here's a short-form addendum we can attach to the existing MSA:

- Scope: 48-hour priority burst window (2028-03-06 00:00:00 UTC to 2028-03-08 00:00:00 UTC) for Sundial Health account RDW-4857
- Commitment: reserved token pool sized to customer-provided peak profile; Redwood guarantees p95 latency for tokens served from the pool (p95 < 220ms) and an availability target of 99.9% for the window
- Pricing: fixed uplift fee equal to 25% of the monthly committed usage, billed pro rata for the 48-hour period (we can provide exact number once pool size is confirmed)
- Sign-off: DocuSign link below for a one-click acceptance; addendum becomes effective on execution

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/RDW-4857/addendum

Procurement: if you need a formal quote or internal PO wording, I can generate that today. If you'd like the uplift to include dedicated telemetry retention for 90 days, that's an additional line item.

-Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdw_sla_addendum_v1.docx

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary throughput uplift for launch week

Thanks all — this looks reasonable. A couple of asks from Sundial procurement and SRE before we sign:
1) Can Redwood pre-populate the pool sizing based on our attached traffic_report_q1.csv? If so, please send the exact token/sec numbers and the expected uplift cost.
2) We need an explicit statement on how fairshare rules will be applied during the uplift window (we don't want our pilot traffic to be subject to late-stage preemption).
3) Procurement requests a 72-hour expedited turnaround on the DocuSign approval once you upload the final addendum. We can sign immediately if those three items are satisfied.

If you can get the pre-populated sizing and the fairshare statement to me by EOD today (PST), procurement will be able to execute within 72 hours.

Appreciate the fast response — looking forward to getting this in place for launch.

Alex Rivera
Director of Platform Engineering
Sundial Health

On Fri, Mar 2, 2028 at 08:39 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — quick note from the contracts side...

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@sundialhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary throughput uplift & SLA addendum for Sundial Health

Alex — we populated sizing against your CSV and recommend a priority pool of 10,000 tokens/sec with a 2-minute burst allowance to meet the 6k req/min peak profile you described. Estimated uplift fee for the 48-hour window is $6,250 (prorated).

Fairshare statement (short): During the priority pool window, requests served from the reserved pool are insulated from standard fairshare preemption; Redwood will not demote or preempt tokens assigned to the reserved pool except in catastrophic platform-wide failure events, in which case Redwood will trigger the outage SLA. All other traffic remains subject to normal fairness policies.

I've uploaded the finalized addendum to DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/RDW-4857/addendum (you should see an email from DocuSign shortly). Per your request we'll aim for a 72-hour review turnaround from upload.

If this matches what you need, please confirm and procurement can sign.

-David
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdw_sla_addendum_v1.docx
